clue.text: Computer program upset animal

parts.note: an app is a program for a phone or computer

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a camel is the animal intended

explanation.surface: A piece of software has upset some creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apple Mac is a well-known brand of personal computer, so the brand name stands for the machine.

clue.text: Coach supporting Brockwell's foot

indicators.note: in a down entry, a supporting piece sits underneath the one it holds up

parts.note: the setter Brockwell speaking of himself says 'I am'
a coach is a bus

explanation.surface: A coach is propping up the setter's foot, as if after an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by their pseudonym, so 'Brockwell's' is read as 'Brockwell is', the setter saying I AM. The foot is a metrical one, not a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: An iambus is a metrical foot of one unstressed then one stressed syllable in verse.

clue.text: Served up posh fish sauce

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means brought upwards, so the letters run from the bottom

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A waiter serves fish with an upmarket sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragu is an Italian meat sauce served with pasta, a hyponym of the general word for a sauce.

clue.text: Woman laid out case for new idea

indicators.note: things laid out are spread and arranged afresh, so the letters are rearranged
a case is the outside of something, so only the outermost letters of the next word are kept

parts.note: the two outside letters of new
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman presents her argument for a fresh idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwina is a female given name, so any woman bearing it fits the bare definition.

clue.text: Got sick catching mad cow disease, headed for rock bottom

indicators.note: to catch something is to take it inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: ailed means was ill
BSE is the abbreviation for bovine spongiform encephalopathy

explanation.surface: Someone fell ill with BSE and their life went downhill fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headed for rock bottom' reads as decline, but it literally describes descending a cliff face on a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Abseiling is descending a rock face by rope, literally going down towards the bottom of the rock.

clue.text: Smooth tenor's song for Universal Studios?

parts.note: to plane wood is to make it smooth
T is the abbreviation for tenor
an aria is an operatic song

explanation.surface: A smooth-voiced tenor sings a number for the Hollywood film company.
explanation.walkthrough: Universal Studios is the film company; read literally, it means places for studying the universe, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Planetaria are domed theatres where the night sky and cosmos are projected and studied, plural of planetarium.

clue.text: African runner's high-tech leg work

indicators.note: high here means intoxicated, and a befuddled word gets its letters jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
to go is to work or function, as in 'the engine won't go'

explanation.surface: An African sprinter attributes success to high-tech training on the legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but in crosswords a runner is often a river. The hyphen in high-tech hides the split between indicator and fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Congo is a great river of central Africa, and a river is a crossword runner because it flows.

clue.text: Author's cat regurgitated fluff

parts.note: the author of the clue refers to himself as me

indicators.note: regurgitated food comes back up the way it went down, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: puss is a familiar name for a cat

explanation.surface: The writer's cat has coughed up a fur ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluff' looks like the hairball the cat brings up, but it is a verb meaning to bungle.
explanation.definitionFit: To fluff a task is to bungle it, the same as making a hash of it.

clue.text: Notice a WAG following the face of Premier League

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this pair goes behind the other letters
a face is the front of something, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Premier
L is the abbreviation for league
taken as written
a wag or card is a joker, a witty person

explanation.surface: A footballer's wife or girlfriend sticks up a sign about the Premier League.
explanation.walkthrough: WAG is tabloid shorthand for a footballer's wife or girlfriend, but here it is a joker.
explanation.definitionFit: A placard is a sign or poster displayed in public, so it is a notice.

clue.text: Bloody-minded husband that is next to good-for-nothing in retirement

indicators.note: next to means beside, so the two parts sit side by side
retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a slob is a lazy good-for-nothing
H is the abbreviation for husband
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A stubborn husband dozes beside a retired idler.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshie is British informal for obstinately uncooperative, from Bolshevik, so it means deliberately awkward.

clue.text: Dog belonging to us has brief thing for 18ac

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a lab is a Labrador retriever
our means belonging to us
an item is a thing

explanation.surface: Our dog has a brief fondness for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 18ac is RED, a left-winger; a Labourite supports Britain's left-of-centre Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is a byword for left-wing politics, and a supporter of the Labour Party is broadly a leftist.

clue.text: Kisses the ultimate in frogs after drink

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other

parts.note: to neck a drink is to gulp it down

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so only the final letter of the following word counts

parts.note: the final letter of frogs

explanation.surface: After a drink, someone kisses frogs, the fairy-tale route to a prince.
explanation.definitionFit: To neck is informal for to kiss and cuddle, so necks matches kisses as a verb.

clue.text: Slim actress playing TV detective

indicators.note: playing about with letters moves them into new positions

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A slender actress is cast as a television sleuth.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Scarlet is the Victorian sleuth heroine of the BBC series Miss Scarlet and the Duke.

clue.text: Layer of skin almost eaten by venom-producing pest

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside the eater, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: spite is venomous malice

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the dermis is the layer of skin under the epidermis

explanation.surface: A poisonous bug gnaws away at the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Venom-producing' looks like one adjective; the hyphen hides the split between the venom of the wordplay and the link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The spider mite is a tiny arachnid that infests plants, a notorious garden and greenhouse pest.

clue.text: Father Brown finally going back to sleep

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the letters read right to left

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of Brown

explanation.surface: G. K. Chesterton's priest-detective Father Brown nods off at last.
explanation.definitionFit: A nap is a short sleep, so the noun nap fits sleep as a noun.

clue.text: Animal found in Mexico at intervals

indicators.note: found in says the answer is sitting inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the next two

explanation.surface: A creature that turns up now and then in Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At intervals' tempts you to take alternate letters, but it is just part of the text in which the answer hides.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a raccoon-like mammal of the Americas, found in Mexico among other places.

clue.text: Rishton's opener in beer match is most watchful

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

indicators.note: an opener is what starts things off, so the initial letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of Rishton
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: A Lancashire cricket club's opening batter stays alert while drinking in a beer match.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishton is a Lancashire League cricket club; its opener suggests a batter, but it only supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Alertest is the superlative of alert, meaning most vigilant, so it matches most watchful.

clue.text: Revolutionary article in Bild is retracted

indicators.note: retracted means drawn back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: der is a German definite article, and Bild is a German newspaper

explanation.surface: A radical story in a German tabloid gets withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Bild is a German tabloid, which points to a German word for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is the colour and nickname of communist revolutionaries, as in the Red Army.

clue.text: On Beauty by Zadie essentially resisted authority

parts.note: re means on or about
a belle is a beautiful woman

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its heart, so the central letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of Zadie

explanation.surface: Zadie Smith's novel On Beauty, at its heart, is about defying authority.
explanation.walkthrough: On Beauty is a novel by Zadie Smith, so the title looks like a single unit; it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebel is to rise up against those in power, so rebelled means resisted authority.

clue.text: Drink in Kai Havertz's agreement to join City

indicators.note: joining puts one piece onto the end of the other

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a city
Kai Havertz is a German footballer, and ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: A German footballer agrees to sign for Manchester City over a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' looks like the football club; it is just any city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine from the Rioja region of Spain, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Acoustic from Oasis's No.1 track under scrutiny

indicators.note: in a down entry, under places these letters below the others

parts.note: an audit is a close examination

indicators.note: number one is the first, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of Oasis
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: An acoustic version of Oasis's top hit comes under close examination.
explanation.walkthrough: Oasis is a British rock band, and a No.1 track sounds like a chart-topper; both are broken up for letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Acoustic and auditory both mean relating to sound or the sense of hearing.

clue.text: Make out with date

definitions.meaning: first meaning: discern with the eyes
second meaning: go out with someone romantically

explanation.surface: Kissing and cuddling with a romantic partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make out' suggests kissing, but it means discern.
explanation.definitionFit: To see is to perceive visually, and seeing someone also means being in a romantic relationship with them.

clue.text: World In Motion saving department in hospital

indicators.note: saving means keeping safe within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital

indicators.note: read as depart-ment, it tells a letter to leave the word it sits in

parts.note: a turn is a movement or rotation

explanation.surface: New Order's football anthem World In Motion rescues a hospital department.
explanation.walkthrough: Tentative parse: SAN, short for sanatorium, holds TURN shorn of its N. World In Motion was England's 1990 World Cup song by New Order.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is a planet, and in crosswords world is a frequent synonym for any planet.

clue.text: 18ac drunk beers with madras

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Red-faced after drinking beer with a hot madras curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 18ac is RED, as in red-faced; a madras is a hot curry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being red in the face goes with feeling ashamed, so blushing red stands for awkward self-consciousness.

clue.text: Footballer's single covered by Keane?

indicators.note: what is covered is enclosed, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: Roy Keane is the former Manchester United captain, so a Keane may be a Roy
single means one

explanation.surface: Is the footballer's hit record a cover of a Keane song?
explanation.walkthrough: Keane is also a rock band, so a single covered by Keane sounds like a song; the question mark flags Keane as an example of a Roy.
explanation.definitionFit: Wayne Rooney is a famous England and Manchester United footballer.

clue.text: Tense after sailor on board kicks off

indicators.note: being on a ship means being aboard it, so these letters go inside the vessel

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the crossword's usual ship: being 'on board' means inside it

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A tense sailor on deck starts a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' reads as aboard ship; crosswords write a ship as SS, steamship, and put things on board inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To start something is to begin it, and kicks off is an informal phrase for begins.

clue.text: Time of the month initially cramping the belly of sex symbol

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: cramping means squeezing in, so one piece is held inside the others
initially points to the first letters of the words concerned

parts.note: the first letters of these three words
the middle letter of sex

explanation.surface: Period pains at the time of the month, and a sex symbol's stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time of the month' reads as a period, and 'sex symbol' as one phrase; only 'symbol' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or emblem revered as a symbol of a clan or group.

clue.text: Brave warrior injured Latin hero

indicators.note: an injured thing is broken and out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A courageous fighter wounds a classical Roman hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A lionheart is a person of great courage, as in King Richard I, the crusader king called the Lionheart.

clue.text: Commander of the Admiralty

indicators.note: of here means made from, so the answer is formed from part of the next words

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: The chief officer of the Royal Navy's governing body.
explanation.definitionFit: A head is the person in charge, so a commander or chief of an organisation.

clue.text: Got out of bed with energy to tackle Times Prize

indicators.note: to tackle is to grab hold of, so the pieces wrap around the other letters

parts.note: rose means got up
E is the physics symbol for energy
each T stands for times, as in multiplication

explanation.surface: Someone got up full of energy to have a go at the Times Prize crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times Prize' looks like the newspaper's prize puzzle; the words belong to different parts of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a rosette-shaped ribbon badge awarded as a prize at shows and competitions.

clue.text: One performing rhubarb stick twirls

indicators.note: something that twirls spins round, so the letters face the other way

parts.note: rhubarb and rot both mean nonsense
a cane is a stick

explanation.surface: A performer twirls a rhubarb stalk like a baton.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhubarb is also what extras mutter on stage to sound like a crowd, which fits the performing surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An enactor is someone who acts out or carries out a role, so a performer.
